description: Executor-scale S3 AP access test from Databricks-managed VPC with VPC Peering and Instance Profile

dns_resolution.interpretation: S3 AP alias DNS resolves correctly to S3 endpoint IP

vpc_peering_tcp_443.interpretation: FSx management IP unreachable via VPC Peering — egress restricted by Databricks-managed VPC

vpc_peering_nfs_2049.interpretation: NFS port unreachable via VPC Peering — consistent with Part 2 article findings

s3_ap_access.interpretation: S3 AP request reaches S3 endpoint but FSx backend connection times out. S3 Gateway Endpoint routes to S3 service but FSx for ONTAP S3 AP requires backend connectivity that is blocked.

s3_regular_listbuckets.interpretation: Instance Profile works (IMDS accessible, credentials valid) but policy only allows S3 AP operations, not ListBuckets. This confirms Instance Profile is functional.

imds_access.interpretation: Instance Profile credentials available on cluster node via IMDSv2

conclusion.root_cause: Databricks-managed VPC egress restrictions prevent FSx for ONTAP S3 AP backend connectivity. VPC Peering is established and routes are configured, but cluster-side egress is governed by Databricks-managed security controls.
conclusion.consistency_with_article: Fully consistent with Part 2 findings: Databricks-managed VPC blocks both direct IP (NFS/HTTPS) and S3 AP backend connectivity to FSx for ONTAP.
conclusion.next_step: Requires Customer-managed VPC workspace (same VPC as FSx for ONTAP) for executor-scale validation. This workspace creation is pending Databricks support ticket resolution.
